title: SMP optimization as primary design target
decision: Optimize the system for high throughput multitasking SMP operation, using large transistor budget to improve total system performance
alternatives_or_rejected: Optimize primarily for uniprocessor single-thread peak
rationale: Servers by nature process disparate information with multiple processes active concurrently; paper states system must be optimized for SMP where transistors improve total system performance
outcome: Two processor cores per chip sharing unified L2 via CIU, multi-chip module forming 8-way, four MCMs forming 32-way SMP via Distributed Switch

title: Full system design approach vs chip-only design
where_in_paper: 2. Guiding Principles - Full system design approach
decision: Design entire system from processor to memory and I/O bridge chips together, with marriage to process technology and packaging
alternatives_or_rejected: Designing processor chip in isolation and adding subsystem later
rationale: To optimize the system and allow software to exploit technology, a new high performance processor needs a new subsystem to effectively feed it
outcome: POWER4 defined as technology including chip, L3 directory on chip with off-chip L3, fabric controller, GX controller, chip-to-chip and MCM-to-MCM buses that scale with processor frequency

title: Very high frequency design via logic regularization
where_in_paper: 2. Guiding Principles - Very high frequency design
decision: Revamp chip design with new transistor-level tools and transform complex control logic into regular data flow constructs, preserve system balance as technology allows higher frequencies
alternatives_or_rejected: Retain traditional random control logic and fixed bus frequencies that would unbalance system as frequency increases
rationale: Maintain leadership position with best-of-breed operating frequencies; regular dataflow enables timing closure at GHz range
outcome: Buses except JTAG scale with processor frequency; system can be offered at multiple frequencies and scale proportionately

title: Pervasive RAS eliminating checkstops
where_in_paper: 2. Guiding Principles - Leadership RAS and Section 1 Introduction RAS philosophy
decision: Make RAS pervasive, not just ECC on major arrays; provide redundancy where errors cannot be eliminated and transform hard machine checkstops into synchronous machine interrupts where possible
alternatives_or_rejected: Achieve reliability only by choosing reliable parts and adding ECC to major arrays, allowing hard checkstops
rationale: Servers have evolved to continuous operation where outages of any kind are not tolerated; design must eliminate outages and allow software to circumvent problems
outcome: Trace and debug for First Failure Data Capture, BIST, Performance Monitor, SP interface, POR sequencing, Error Detection and Logging pervasive functions on chip

title: Maintain 32-bit and 64-bit binary compatibility
decision: Maintain absolute binary compatibility for both 32-bit and 64-bit applications with prior PowerPC and PowerPC-AS systems
alternatives_or_rejected: Introduce new ISA or break compatibility for frequency/performance gains
rationale: Internal task forces concluded PowerPC architecture had no technical impediments to scale to significantly higher frequencies with excellent performance, so no technical reason to change and customer software investment must be preserved
outcome: Single POWER4 design satisfies both pSeries and iSeries needs, convergence of iSeries and pSeries microprocessors
